name: Jira Comment Write
description: Contributes the ability to POST a comment to a Jira issue, satisfying the core hard rule that ticketing-system writes arrive only via a module that explicitly grants them. Posting is TPM-only, never autonomous, and always gated on the operator approving the exact comment text. Post only — no editing, deleting, transitioning, or issue creation.
author: aarbuckle

attributionSuffix.label: Attribution Suffix
attributionSuffix.default:
---
Posted via Ghola on behalf of the ticket owner.
attributionSuffix.description: Appended verbatim to every comment this module posts, so a teammate reading the ticket can tell the comment was agent-authored rather than typed by a person. Shown to the operator as part of the approval preview, since it is part of what gets posted. Set to an empty string to disable attribution entirely — not recommended, as unattributed agent comments on a shared ticket are a transparency problem, and the operator is the one whose name is on the account.

requireOperatorApproval.label: Require Operator Approval
requireOperatorApproval.description: When on, TPM must show the operator the full, final comment text and receive an explicit confirmation before posting. This is the module's central safety gate and should be left on. It exists as a setting only so the value is visible and auditable in the panel; turning it off removes the last check between a drafted comment and a permanent, publicly-visible write on a shared ticket, and no workflow in this module is designed to run without it.

commentPolishPrompt.label: Comment Polish Prompt
commentPolishPrompt.default: Write a concise, professional Jira comment stating the update plainly. No hedging, no double-dashes, no severity ratings.
commentPolishPrompt.description: The instruction TPM applies when drafting a comment body from raw session material (a SWE report, a QA verdict, a status update). Governs tone and shape only — it never changes the approval gate, and the operator always sees and approves the final text the prompt produced.
